label: r4c2
name: slim stem, compute ratio about 1
hypothesis: Only change from r3c2: the stem shrinks (STEM 64 to 32, COL 48 to 40), bringing the compute ratio from about 1.21 to about 1.0. That gives about 20% more fresh samples and gradient steps. r3c2's curve was still rising, and widening the stem (r2c2) gave no clear gain, so stem width looks cheap to cut. Refuted if 2-seed dev success is at or below about 0.87, which would mean the stem's capacity mattered more than the extra samples.
last_analysis: The circular full-row stem is what made learning possible, because it lets each cell see the target shifted 4 columns away. Without it, or with the learned column warp in r1c3, every trial collapsed to choosing DONE on the first step. Adding global context to the placement head helped (0.70 to 0.74). Recipe changes have mattered most since then. 64 minibatches gave 0.78. Using 1 epoch with 64 minibatches (r3c2) gave 0.89, with both seeds close (0.887 and 0.897). So the run is short of samples, and its learning curve was still rising at the end (0.77 to 0.82). The full footprint conv (r3c3, 0.54) and the wider stem (r2c2, 0.715 against 0.697) did not help, which suggests extra per-cell capacity is not the bottleneck. This is the last round, so all three candidates keep r3c2's architecture and recipe. One makes the network cheaper so that the training-compute ratio r is about 1, for about 20% more samples. One raises gamma so the +1 bonus for an exact build counts for more. The third combines both.
